newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Almaz says PGM export talks have started.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Almaz says PGM export talks have started.

text.p: Russia's platinum group metals export agency Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz) said in a statement on Tuesday it had started talks with clients on 1997 exports of platinum and palladium, including with Japan, the biggest buyer.
It also said deliveries to Japan should start by the middle of June, and that it had enough palladium to satisfy customers' needs this year.

"We confirm that we have already started 1997 negotiations," the statement said. It was signed by Almaz's director of platinum group metals (PGMs) department Vitaly Berlin. Berlin told Reuters that the talks included negotiations with Japan.

The statement referred to the sharp increase of speculative demand in the palladium market and said,"... we confirm that the quantities of palladium for 1997 are sufficient enough to satisfy our clients' requirements and to keep palladium prices at a reasonable level."
"Deliveries to Japan should start in the second half of June at the latest," a spokesman for Almaz said.

Russia is the world's largest palladium supplier and second largest platinum supplier, and Japan is the largest consumer of both. Long delays in Russian deliveries this year sent palladium prices to two-year highs on Monday.
